sanskrit: saubhadras tu tataḥ śaṅkhaṃ pradhmāpya puruṣarṣabhaḥ śīghram abhyapatat senāṃ bhāratīṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then Subhadrā's son, that bull among men, blew his conch and swiftly fell upon the army of the Bhāratas, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa kakṣe 'gnir ivotsṛṣṭo nirdahaṃs tarasā ripūn madhye bhāratasainyānām ārjuniḥ paryavartata
english: Like fire let loose in dry brush, consuming his foes with sudden force, Arjuna's son ranged through the midst of the Bhārata host.

sanskrit: rathanāgāśvamanujān ardayan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sa praviśyākarod bhūmiṃ kabandhagaṇasaṃkulām
english: Tormenting chariots, elephants, horses, and men with his whetted shafts, he plunged in and made the earth thick with throngs of headless trunks.

sanskrit: saubhadracāpaprabhavair nikṛttāḥ parameṣubhiḥ svān evābhimukhān ghnantaḥ prādravañ jīvitārthinaḥ
english: Cut down by the matchless arrows sprung from Subhadrā's son's bow, men fled in their longing for life, striking even their own comrades who faced them.

sanskrit: te ghorā raudrakarmāṇo vipāṭhāḥ pṛthavaḥ śitāḥ nighnanto rathanāgāśvāñ jagmur āśu vasuṃdharām
english: Those dreadful broad-headed shafts, sharp and terrible in their work, slew chariots, elephants, and horses, and swiftly buried themselves in the earth.

sanskrit: sāyudhāḥ sāṅgulitrāṇāḥ sakhaḍgāḥ sāṅgadā raṇe dṛśyante bāhavaś chinnā hemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: In that battle there could be seen severed arms, still gripping weapons, still wearing finger-guards, swords, and armlets, adorned with golden ornaments.

sanskrit: śarāś cāpāni khaḍgāś ca śarīrāṇi śirāṃsi ca sakuṇḍalāni sragvīṇi bhūmāv āsan sahasraśaḥ
english: Arrows and bows and swords, bodies and heads—wearing earrings and garlands—lay upon the ground by the thousands.

sanskrit: apaskarair adhiṣṭhānair īṣādaṇḍakabandhuraiḥ akṣair vimathitaiś cakrair bhagnaiś ca bahudhā rathaiḥ śakticāpāyudhaiś cāpi patitaiś ca mahādhvajaiḥ
english: With wheel-frames and floor-boards, with poles, shafts, and seat-rails, with shattered axles and broken wheels, with chariots smashed in many ways, with spears, bows, and weapons, and with great fallen banners—

sanskrit: nihataiḥ kṣatriyair aśvair vāraṇaiś ca viśāṃ pate agamyakalpā pṛthivī kṣaṇenāsīt sudāruṇā
english: with slain warriors, horses, and elephants, O lord of peoples, in a moment the earth became all but impassable and most fearsome to behold.

sanskrit: vadhyatāṃ rājaputrāṇāṃ krandatām itaretaram prādurāsīn mahāśabdo bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanaḥ sa śabdo bharataśreṣṭha diśaḥ sarvā vyanādayat
english: From the princes being slaughtered, crying out to one another, there arose a mighty din that swelled the terror of the timid; and that sound, O best of the Bhāratas, made all the quarters resound.

sanskrit: saubhadraś cādravat senāṃ nighnann aśvarathadvipān vyacarat sa diśaḥ sarvāḥ pradiśaś cāhitān rujan
english: Subhadrā's son charged the army, striking down horses, chariots, and elephants; he ranged through all the quarters and the intermediate quarters, crushing the foe.

sanskrit: taṃ tadā nānupaśyāma sainyena rajasāvṛtam ādadānaṃ gajāśvānāṃ nṛṇāṃ cāyūṃṣi bhārata
english: We could not then make him out, veiled by the army's dust as he took the lives of elephants, horses, and men, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena bhūyo 'paśyāma sūryaṃ madhyaṃdine yathā abhimanyuṃ mahārāja pratapantaṃ dviṣadgaṇān
english: In a moment we saw him again, O great king, like the noonday sun—Abhimanyu, scorching the hosts of his enemies.

sanskrit: sa vāsavasamaḥ saṃkhye vāsavasyātmajātmajaḥ abhimanyur mahārāja sainyamadhye vyarocata
english: Equal to Vāsava in battle, the son of Vāsava's son's son, Abhimanyu, O great king, shone resplendent in the midst of the army.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bālam atyantasukhinam avāryabaladarpitam yuddheṣu kuśalaṃ vīraṃ kulaputraṃ tanutyajam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A boy, reared in utter ease, proud with irresistible strength, skilled in battle, a hero, a scion of a noble house, ready to lay down his life—

sanskrit: gāhamānam anīkāni sadaśvais taṃ trihāyanaiḥ api yaudhiṣṭhirāt sainyāt kaś cid anvapatad rathī
english: as he plunged into the ranks with his fine three-year-old steeds, did any chariot-warrior from Yudhiṣṭhira's army follow after him?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yudhiṣṭhiro bhīmasenaḥ śikhaṇḍī sātyakir yamau dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca sakekayaḥ dhṛṣṭaketuś ca saṃrabdho matsyāś cānvapatan raṇe
english: Saṃjaya said: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīmasena, Śikhaṇḍin, Sātyaki, the twins, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa, Drupada with the Kekayas, the furious Dhṛṣṭaketu, and the Matsyas followed after him into the battle.

sanskrit: abhyadravan parīpsanto vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ tān dṛṣṭvā dravataḥ śūrāṃs tvadīyā vimukhābhavan
english: In their eagerness to protect him those smiters charged, their ranks arrayed; and seeing those heroes rushing on, your men turned their faces away.

sanskrit: tatas tad vimukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tava sūnor mahad balam jāmātā tava tejasvī viṣṭambhayiṣur ādravat
english: Then, seeing the great host of your son turned away, your splendid son-in-law charged forward, resolved to hold the line.

sanskrit: saindhavasya mahārāja putro rājā jayadrathaḥ sa putragṛddhinaḥ pārthān sahasainyān avārayat
english: The king Jayadratha, son of the lord of the Sindhus, O great king, held back the sons of Pṛthā together with their army as they pressed on, hungry to reach their son.

sanskrit: ugradhanvā maheṣvāso divyam astram udīrayan vārdhakṣatrir upāsedhat pravaṇād iva kuñjarān
english: Of dreadful bow, a great archer, the son of Vṛddhakṣatra invoked a divine weapon and checked them, as one checks elephants charging down a slope.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca atibhāram ahaṃ manye saindhave saṃjayāhitam yad ekaḥ pāṇḍavān kruddhān putragṛddhīn avārayat
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A burden too great, I think, was laid upon the lord of the Sindhus, Saṃjaya, in that alone he held back the wrathful Pāṇḍavas longing to reach their son.

sanskrit: atyadbhutam idaṃ manye balaṃ śauryaṃ ca saindhave tad asya brūhi me vīryaṃ karma cāgryaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Most wondrous, I deem, are the strength and valor in the lord of the Sindhus. Tell me then of that great soul's prowess and his foremost deed.

sanskrit: kiṃ dattaṃ hutam iṣṭaṃ vā sutaptam atha vā tapaḥ sindhurājena yenaikaḥ kruddhān pārthān avārayat
english: What did the king of the Sindhus give, or offer in oblation, or sacrifice, or what austerity did he duly perform, that alone he could hold back the wrathful sons of Pṛthā?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca draupadīharaṇe yat tad bhīmasenena nirjitaḥ mānāt sa taptavān rājā varārthī sumahat tapaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When, at the carrying off of Draupadī, that king was vanquished by Bhīmasena, then out of wounded pride, seeking a boon, he performed exceedingly severe austerity.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyaḥ priyebhyaḥ saṃnivartya saḥ kṣutpipāsātapasahaḥ kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ devam ārādhayac charvaṃ gṛṇan brahma sanātanam
english: Drawing back his senses from their dear objects, enduring hunger, thirst, and heat, grown lean, his veins standing forth, he worshipped the god Śarva, reciting the eternal sacred word.

sanskrit: bhaktānukampī bhagavāṃs tasya cakre tato dayām svapnānte 'py atha caivāha haraḥ sindhupateḥ sutam varaṃ vṛṇīṣva prīto 'smi jayadratha kim icchasi
english: The Lord, compassionate to his devotees, then took pity on him; and at the end of a dream Hara said to the son of the lord of the Sindhus: 'Choose a boon, I am pleased, Jayadratha—what do you desire?'

sanskrit: evam uktas tu śarveṇa sindhurājo jayadrathaḥ uvāca praṇato rudraṃ prāñjalir niyatātmavān
english: So addressed by Śarva, Jayadratha, king of the Sindhus, bowing low before Rudra with joined palms, his soul composed, replied:

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveyān ahaṃ saṃkhye bhīmavīryaparākramān eko raṇe dhārayeyaṃ samastān iti bhārata
english: 'May I, alone in battle, hold back the sons of Pāṇḍu, of terrible valor and might, all of them together'—so he prayed, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu deveśo jayadratham athābravīt dadāmi te varaṃ saumya vinā pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: So addressed, the lord of the gods then said to Jayadratha: 'I grant you the boon, gentle one—save only Pṛthā's son Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: dhārayiṣyasi saṃgrāme caturaḥ pāṇḍunandanān evam astv iti deveśam uktvābudhyata pārthivaḥ
english: In battle you shall hold back the four sons of Pāṇḍu.' Saying 'So be it' to the lord of the gods, the king awoke.

sanskrit: sa tena varadānena divyenāstrabalena ca ekaḥ saṃdhārayām āsa pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: By that granting of the boon and by the power of his divine weapon, he alone held back the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tasya jyātalaghoṣeṇa kṣatriyān bhayam āviśat parāṃs tu tava sainyasya harṣaḥ paramako 'bhavat
english: At the twang of his bowstring and the slap of his palm, fear entered the warriors of the foe, while in your army there arose the highest joy.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu kṣatriyā bhāraṃ saindhave sarvam arpitam utkruśyābhyadravan rājan yena yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ balam
english: And seeing the whole burden laid upon the lord of the Sindhus, the warriors, raising a shout, charged, O king, against Yudhiṣṭhira's host.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yan mā pṛcchasi rājendra sindhurājasya vikramam śṛṇu tat sarvam ākhyāsye yathā pāṇḍūn ayodhayat
english: Saṃjaya said: As to the valor of the king of the Sindhus about which you ask me, O king of kings—hear it; I shall tell it all, how he fought the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tam ūhuḥ sārather vaśyāḥ saindhavāḥ sādhuvāhinaḥ vikurvāṇā bṛhanto 'śvāḥ śvasanopamaraṃhasaḥ
english: Him the great Sindhu horses bore on, obedient to the charioteer, well-trained and high-mettled, prancing, swift as the wind.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākāraṃ vidhivat kalpitaṃ ratham tasyābhyaśobhayat ketur vārāho rājato mahān
english: His chariot, fashioned according to rule and shaped like a Gandharva's city, was adorned by a banner bearing a great silver boar.

sanskrit: śvetacchatrapatākābhiś cāmaravyajanena ca sa babhau rājaliṅgais tais tārāpatir ivāmbare
english: With white parasol and pennants and with whisk and fan, he shone forth in those marks of royalty like the lord of the stars in the sky.

sanskrit: muktāvajramaṇisvarṇair bhūṣitaṃ tad ayasmayam varūthaṃ vibabhau tasya jyotirbhiḥ kham ivāvṛtam
english: Adorned with pearls, diamonds, gems, and gold, his iron fender shone like the firmament strewn with stars.

sanskrit: sa visphārya mahac cāpaṃ kirann iṣugaṇān bahūn tat khaṇḍaṃ pūrayām āsa yad vyadārayad ārjuniḥ
english: Twanging his great bow and scattering many showers of shafts, he filled up that gap which the son of Arjuna had torn open.

sanskrit: sa sātyakiṃ tribhir bāṇair aṣṭabhiś ca vṛkodaram dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tathā ṣaṣṭyā virāṭaṃ daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: He pierced Sātyaki with three arrows, Vṛkodara with eight, Dhṛṣṭadyumna with sixty, and Virāṭa with ten shafts;

sanskrit: drupadaṃ pañcabhis tīkṣṇair daśabhiś ca śikhaṇḍinam kekayān pañcaviṃśatyā draupadeyāṃs tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Drupada with five keen ones, and Śikhaṇḍin with ten, the Kekayas with twenty-five, and the sons of Draupadī with three apiece;

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca saptatyā tataḥ śeṣān apānudat iṣujālena mahatā tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: and Yudhiṣṭhira with seventy; then he drove off the rest with a vast web of arrows—a thing that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: athāsya śitapītena bhallenādiśya kārmukam ciccheda prahasan rājā dharmaputraḥ pratāpavān
english: Then, taking aim at his bow with a sharp, gold-bright broad-headed shaft, the mighty King Yudhiṣṭhira, the Dharma-born, laughing, cut it in two.

sanskrit: akṣṇor nimeṣamātreṇa so 'nyad ādāya kārmukam vivyādha daśabhiḥ pārtha tāṃś caivānyāṃs tribhis tribhiḥ
english: In but the twinkling of an eye he took up another bow and pierced him with ten shafts, O Pārtha, and the others, each with three.

sanskrit: tasya tal lāghavaṃ jñātvā bhīmo bhallais tribhiḥ punaḥ dhanur dhvajaṃ ca chatraṃ ca kṣitau kṣipram apātayat
english: Marking that lightness of hand, Bhīma with three broad-headed shafts swiftly brought down to the ground his bow, his banner, and his parasol.

sanskrit: so 'nyad ādāya balavān sajyaṃ kṛtvā ca kārmukam bhīmasyāpothayat ketuṃ dhanur aśvāṃś ca māriṣa
english: The strong one, taking up another bow and stringing it, shattered Bhīma's banner, bow, and horses, O honored one.

sanskrit: sa hatāśvād avaplutya chinnadhanvā rathottamāt sātyaker āpluto yānaṃ giryagram iva kesarī
english: His horses slain and his bow cut through, Bhīma leapt down from his splendid car and sprang onto Sātyaki's chariot, like a lion onto a mountain peak.

sanskrit: tatas tvadīyāḥ saṃhṛṣṭāḥ sādhu sādhv iti cukruśuḥ sindhurājasya tat karma prekṣyāśraddheyam uttamam
english: Then your men, exulting, cried out 'Well done! Well done!' beholding that supreme and scarcely credible feat of the king of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: saṃkruddhān pāṇḍavān eko yad dadhārāstratejasā tat tasya karma bhūtāni sarvāṇy evābhyapūjayan
english: That he alone, by the splendor of his weapons, held back the wrathful Pāṇḍavas—at that deed of his all beings did him homage.

sanskrit: saubhadreṇa hataiḥ pūrvaṃ sottarāyudhibhir dvipaiḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ darśitaḥ panthāḥ saindhavena nivāritaḥ
english: The path opened for the Pāṇḍavas by the elephants—with their riders and weapons—earlier slain by Subhadrā's son, was now barred by the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: yatamānās tu te vīrā matsyapāñcālakekayāḥ pāṇḍavāś cānvapadyanta pratyaikaśyena saindhavam
english: Though those heroes strove—the Matsyas, the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, and the Pāṇḍavas—they came against the lord of the Sindhus only one by one.

sanskrit: yo yo hi yatate bhettuṃ droṇānīkaṃ tavāhitaḥ taṃ taṃ devavaraprāptyā saindhavaḥ pratyavārayat
english: Whatever foe of yours strove to break through Droṇa's array, that one the lord of the Sindhus, by virtue of the god's boon, turned back.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saindhavena niruddheṣu jayagṛddhiṣu pāṇḍuṣu sughoram abhavad yuddhaṃ tvadīyānāṃ paraiḥ saha
english: Saṃjaya said: When the sons of Pāṇḍu, hungry for victory, had been checked by the lord of the Sindhus, a most terrible battle arose between your men and the foe.

sanskrit: praviśya tv ārjuniḥ senāṃ satyasaṃdho durāsadām vyakṣobhayata tejasvī makaraḥ sāgaraṃ yathā
english: Having entered that unassailable army, the son of Arjuna, true to his vow and full of splendor, churned it up as a sea-monster churns the ocean.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā śaravarṣeṇa kṣobhayantam ariṃdamam yathāpradhānāḥ saubhadram abhyayuḥ kurusattamāḥ
english: As that tamer of foes, Subhadrā's son, thus churned the host with his rain of arrows, the foremost of the Kurus, each in his rank, advanced upon him.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tasya ca saṃmardo dāruṇaḥ samapadyata sṛjatāṃ śaravarṣāṇi prasaktam amitaujasām
english: A fearsome and unbroken clash came to pass between them and him, as those of measureless might poured forth their showers of arrows.

sanskrit: rathavrajena saṃruddhas tair amitrair athārjuniḥ vṛṣasenasya yantāraṃ hatvā ciccheda kārmukam
english: Hemmed in by that throng of chariots, by those foes, Arjuna's son slew Vṛṣasena's charioteer and cut through his bow.

sanskrit: tasya vivyādha balavāñ śarair aśvān ajihmagaiḥ vātāyamānair atha tair aśvair apahṛto raṇāt
english: The strong one pierced his horses with straight-flying shafts, and by those steeds, now bolting like the wind, Vṛṣasena was carried off from the field.

sanskrit: tenāntareṇābhimanyor yantāpāsārayad ratham rathavrajās tato hṛṣṭāḥ sādhu sādhv iti cukruśuḥ
english: In that interval Abhimanyu's charioteer drove his chariot forward; then the throngs of car-warriors, delighted, cried out 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: taṃ siṃham iva saṃkruddhaṃ pramathnantaṃ śarair arīn ārād āyāntam abhyetya vasātīyo 'bhyayād drutam
english: As he came on from afar, wrathful as a lion, crushing his foes with arrows, the prince of the Vasātis met him and swiftly charged.

sanskrit: so 'bhimanyuṃ śaraiḥ ṣaṣṭyā rukmapuṅkhair avākirat abravīc ca na me jīvañ jīvato yudhi mokṣyase
english: He showered Abhimanyu with sixty gold-feathered shafts and said: 'While I live, you shall not escape from me alive in battle.'

sanskrit: tam ayasmayavarmāṇam iṣuṇā āśupātinā vivyādha hṛdi saubhadraḥ sa papāta vyasuḥ kṣitau
english: Him, clad in iron mail, Subhadrā's son pierced in the heart with a swift-falling arrow, and he fell lifeless to the earth.

sanskrit: vasātyaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā kruddhāḥ kṣatriyapuṃgavāḥ parivavrus tadā rājaṃs tava pautraṃ jighāṃsavaḥ
english: Seeing the Vasāti slain, the bulls among warriors, enraged, then surrounded your grandson, O king, eager to kill him.

sanskrit: visphārayantaś cāpāni nānārūpāṇy anekaśaḥ tad yuddham abhavad raudraṃ saubhadrasyāribhiḥ saha
english: Twanging their bows of many shapes and many kinds, they fought a dreadful battle, the foes against Subhadrā's son.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śarān seṣvasanāñ śarīrāṇi śirāṃsi ca sakuṇḍalāni sragvīṇi kruddhaś ciccheda phālguniḥ
english: Their arrows together with their bows, and their bodies and heads—wearing earrings and garlands—the wrathful son of Phalguna cut asunder.

sanskrit: sakhaḍgāḥ sāṅgulitrāṇāḥ sapaṭṭiśaparaśvadhāḥ adṛśyanta bhujāś chinnā hemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: Severed arms could be seen, still holding swords, finger-guards, spiked maces, and axes, adorned with golden ornaments.

sanskrit: sragbhir ābharaṇair vastraiḥ patitaiś ca mahādhvajaiḥ varmabhiś carmabhir hārair mukuṭaiś chatracāmaraiḥ
english: With garlands, ornaments, and garments, with fallen great banners, with cuirasses, shields, necklaces, diadems, parasols, and whisks—

sanskrit: apaskarair adhiṣṭhānair īṣādaṇḍakabandhuraiḥ akṣair vimathitaiś cakrair bhagnaiś ca bahudhā yugaiḥ
english: with wheel-frames and floor-boards, with poles, shafts, and seat-rails, with shattered axles and broken wheels, with yokes smashed in many ways—

sanskrit: anukarṣaiḥ patākābhis tathā sārathivājibhiḥ rathaiś ca bhagnair nāgaiś ca hataiḥ kīrṇābhavan mahī
english: with under-poles and pennants, with charioteers and steeds, with broken chariots and slain elephants, the earth was strewn.

sanskrit: nihataiḥ kṣatriyaiḥ śūrair nānājanapadeśvaraiḥ jayagṛddhair vṛtā bhūmir dāruṇā samapadyata
english: Covered with slain warriors, heroes, lords of many lands, all hungry for victory, the earth became a fearsome thing.

sanskrit: diśo vicaratas tasya sarvāś ca pradiśas tathā raṇe 'bhimanyoḥ kruddhasya rūpam antaradhīyata
english: As wrathful Abhimanyu ranged through all the quarters and the intermediate quarters in battle, his form vanished from sight.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ yad yad asyāsīd varma cābharaṇāni ca dhanuṣaś ca śarāṇāṃ ca tad apaśyāma kevalam
english: Whatever golden armor and ornaments were his, and the gold of his bow and arrows—that alone could we see.

sanskrit: taṃ tadā nāśakat kaś cic cakṣurbhyām abhivīkṣitum ādadānaṃ śarair yodhān madhye sūryam iva sthitam
english: None then could gaze upon him with his eyes, as he took the warriors' lives with his shafts, standing in their midst like the sun.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ādadānas tu śūrāṇām āyūṃṣy abhavad ārjuniḥ antakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ prāṇān kāla ivāgate
english: Saṃjaya said: Taking the lives of heroes, the son of Arjuna became like the Ender of all beings, like Time itself come to seize their breath.

sanskrit: sa śakra iva vikrāntaḥ śakrasūnoḥ suto balī abhimanyus tadānīkaṃ loḍayan bahv aśobhata
english: Valiant as Śakra, the mighty son of Śakra's son—Abhimanyu—shone surpassingly as he tossed that army into confusion.

sanskrit: praviśyaiva tu rājendra kṣatriyendrāntakopamaḥ satyaśravasam ādatta vyāghro mṛgam ivolbaṇam
english: Having plunged in, O king of kings, like Death to the lords of warriors, he took the life of Satyaśravas, as a tiger takes a fierce deer.

sanskrit: satyaśravasi cākṣipte tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ pragṛhya vipulaṃ śastram abhimanyum upādravan
english: When Satyaśravas had been struck down, the great car-warriors in haste, seizing their broad weapons, rushed upon Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: ahaṃ pūrvam ahaṃ pūrvam iti kṣatriyapuṃgavāḥ spardhamānāḥ samājagmur jighāṃsanto 'rjunātmajam
english: 'I first! I first!'—so vying with one another, the bulls among warriors came on together, bent on slaying Arjuna's son.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇām anīkāni pradrutāny abhidhāvatām jagrāsa timir āsādya kṣudramatsyān ivārṇave
english: The ranks of warriors that came charging on he swallowed up as a great fish in the ocean falls upon and devours the little fish.
